clue.text: Musical demonstration, first of blue grass

parts.note: a show is a demonstration or display

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word blue is taken

parts.note: oats are a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A display of bluegrass music, its first number on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective for the demonstration, but it is the definition, the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Show Boat is the famous Kern and Hammerstein stage musical, so the title names one example.

clue.text: Direct ball over top of goal — both sides admitting I make important miss

indicators.note: in a down entry, this piece sits above the rest

parts.note: to head the ball is to direct it with one's head

indicators.note: the letters let in another piece between them
the first letter of the word goal is taken

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left

explanation.surface: A footballer heads over the bar and misses a big chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a missed chance, but it is a girl: a school's most senior pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British school the senior girl prefect is a leading young lady, a 'miss' of some standing.

clue.text: All agreed one can't sing duets like that

definitions.meaning: unanimously, everyone of the same view

definitions.text: one can't sing duets like that
definitions.meaning: a duet needs two parts, not a single singer

explanation.definitionFit: Speaking unanimously means all agreeing; literally a duet cannot be sung by a single singer.

clue.text: General principles not in actor's text

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
an actor learns lines

explanation.surface: An actor neglects the rules by not learning the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad outlines are the main features or principles of a plan, without detail.

clue.text: Not extravagant disagreement, in your case

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, which serves as its case

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
a rift is a split or disagreement

explanation.surface: In your situation, arguing about money would be thriftless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' pairs with 'in': the archaic word for your is the casing, and the disagreement goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty means careful with money, the opposite of extravagant.

clue.text: Resistance to travel in midwinter, so getting special terms

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the month

parts.note: January, JAN, falls in the middle of the northern winter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
go means travel

explanation.surface: Travelling in deep winter meets resistance, with special terms agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is the specialised vocabulary of a trade or profession.

clue.text: Cringe, seeing lover embrace wif

indicators.note: the lover's letters hug the other piece

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or lover of something
the paper misprints wife here; W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband cringes at seeing a lover hug his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'wif', a typo for 'wife', whose abbreviation W goes inside FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to grovel or cringe servilely before someone.

clue.text: Some number sweetly arranged in Gregorian mode

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A number is sung sweetly in plainchant style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gregorian' suggests chant, but it is the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: New Style is dating by the Gregorian calendar, which replaced the Julian in Britain in 1752.

clue.text: Torrid time PM cut short with gesture

indicators.note: the final letter of the prime minister's name is chopped off

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister in the 1970s
a wave of the hand is a gesture

explanation.surface: A prime minister's stint is curtailed with a farewell gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970-74; 'cut short' drops his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of very hot weather is a torrid period, by straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Blow as rebel receives fine

indicators.note: the rebel's name takes in another piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A rebel is hit with a fine as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler, leader of the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381, is the crossword's stock rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: To waft is to blow gently, as a breeze carries a scent through the air.

clue.text: Showing affection, as card players are

definitions.meaning: couples walking with palms clasped show fondness
players at a card game each have a set of cards in their grip

explanation.definitionFit: Clasping a partner's palm shows fondness, while card players literally keep their dealt cards gripped.

clue.text: Poetic technique nothing but repeats?

parts.note: all, as in 'all talk', means nothing but
iteration is repetition

explanation.surface: A poem's method is said to be mere repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating initial consonant sounds is a standard device of verse.

clue.text: Fighter with no name, in Goethe's poem

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A warplane goes unnamed in a German literary work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a soldier, but it is the MiG jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignon is a lyric by Goethe, the song of the girl in Wilhelm Meister, famous as 'Kennst du das Land'.

clue.text: Came down to bring round award for classical music feature

indicators.note: the award's letters are placed round the other piece

parts.note: a Tony is an American theatre award
alit is the past tense of alight, to come down

explanation.surface: Someone descends to collect a prize for a feature of classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring round' sounds like reviving someone; here it signals the award wrapped round the past tense of alight. A Tony is Broadway's annual theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in a key, major or minor, is a defining characteristic of classical Western music.

clue.text: Generous to son: that's hardly original

parts.note: lavish means generous or unstinting

explanation.surface: A parent is open-handed with a son, and the result is derivative.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish imitation copies without independence, so a slavish work is scarcely original.

clue.text: The scalp, it may appear, is tough

definitions.meaning: the scalp seems to be the covering on top of the cranium
a tough is a thug, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed youth of a violent subculture is a tough; literally the scalp is the covering of the head.

clue.text: Herb received minor wound, gaining exemption from army

indicators.note: the herb takes in the other piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb
a cut is a small wound

explanation.surface: A soldier with a small wound is excused military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' could be a man's name, but it is SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scutage was a medieval payment a knight made to the crown in lieu of military service.

clue.text: Caught in embrace, demanding charity

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hugging, embracing; the noun stands for the action

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a hug is being asked for money.
explanation.walkthrough: Chugging is British slang, from 'charity mugging', for street fundraisers who accost passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Street fundraisers who press passers-by for donations are said to be doing this.

clue.text: Organise gear to record gorilla, say

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: to tape is to record

explanation.surface: Kit is set up to film a gorilla.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is one of the large primates, an example of the group.

clue.text: Deterioration, but I left fruit-tree up

indicators.note: the letter is departed, so removed
in a down entry, the tree is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall

explanation.surface: A trained fruit tree is declining after someone abandoned it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ESPALIER to REILAPSE; 'I left' then takes out the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into a worse state, a deterioration.

clue.text: Friendly hint

definitions.meaning: close and familiar, as an adjective
to suggest indirectly, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means closely familiar; as a verb it means to suggest or imply.

clue.text: Girl's three articles

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl owns three items.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female given name.

clue.text: Pull out tape, maybe, that doesn't sound genuine

parts.note: un- is the negative prefix, saying something does not

indicators.note: the word is judged by how it is spoken, not by its spelling

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: Someone yanks out a tape that seems to be a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreal', not genuine, is said like the answer; 'sound' is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind tape or film from its spool is to draw it out, tape being one example.

clue.text: Where one needn't bend one's efforts any more to win?

definitions.text: Where one needn't bend one's efforts any more to win?

parts.words: Where one needn't bend one's efforts any more to win?
parts.note: on a racetrack the last stretch before the finish has no more curves, so runners need not bend

explanation.definitionFit: The final straight stretch of a racecourse leads to the winning post, with no bends left.

clue.text: Blind group that operate computers

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme's three blind creatures
pointing devices used to control a computer

explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme has three blind rodents, and the plural of a desktop pointing device is the same word.

clue.text: I am a leader of Muslims

definitions.text: I am a leader of Muslims

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Muslims is taken

explanation.surface: A religious leader introduces himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, so is a leader of Muslims.

clue.text: Knowing quality of NHS care, having treatment that's succeeded

indicators.note: the letters are worked on, rearranged as a patient is treated

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The National Health Service is praised for successful treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: NHS is Britain's National Health Service; 'having treatment' rearranges NHS CARE into ARCHNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is a playful, knowing manner, so the noun names that knowing quality.

clue.text: Cause death, drowning in green mixture

indicators.note: one piece is submerged inside the other
the letters of green are mixed up

parts.note: end means death

explanation.surface: Someone causes a death by drowning in a green liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' scrambles the colour word, and 'drowning in' says death sinks inside it; the surface's grisly drowning hides a plain container.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to give rise to or bring about, a synonym of cause as a verb.
